Welcome—I'm glad you're here. Have you ever wondered how your private thoughts might connect to the world around you, or how questioning what you believe could actually deepen your wisdom? Together, we're about to wander through some of life's biggest questions—questions of self, society, and the slippery nature of truth—unfolding in the pages of Michel de Montaigne’s The Complete Essays.
This isn't just a collection of old philosophical musings. Instead, think of it as an open invitation to explore the blurry lines between public and private life, where looking inward actually helps us understand what it means to be human. Montaigne's curiosity, his skepticism, and his raw honesty blend into a journey that touches on everything from morality and friendship, to mortality, and the ever-shifting tides of opinion.
What makes these essays so special? It's the way Montaigne weaves together stories from his own life with bold questions about education, love, custom, and the limits of reason. He invites us into a space where vulnerability and intellect walk hand in hand, where even the simplest details of everyday life become a window into something much deeper.
As we move forward, you and I will step into a conversation that feels both personal and universal—a gentle challenge to our assumptions, and an encouragement to approach the world with more compassion and open-mindedness. So, let’s set out on this journey together, discovering why, in Montaigne’s eyes, it’s often the act of questioning—not the comfort of answers—that gives us our greatest strength and humility.
